item.title: Hear a coach change a race plan
item.summary: A running coach separates route changes from the timing of a group practice.
item.transcript_text: It's going to be hot during Saturday's practice. We'll meet at eight as planned, but turn left at the bridge instead of following the signs for the full course. The shortcut brings us past a public tap at the park. Fill your bottle there even if it is half full. Runners preparing for the ten-kilometre race can add a second loop from the park after everyone has had a drink. Keep to the path by the trees on the second loop. If you have not run with us before, do one loop and tell Jo at the end so we know you are back.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason for the route change?
options: To reduce the length of the real race
To avoid an event at the bridge
To test an unfamiliar start time
To make water accessible on a hot day
questions.explanation: The shortcut passes a public tap in hot conditions.

questions.prompt: What part of the plan stays the same?
options: The turn at the bridge
The route past the tap
The eight o’clock meeting
The number of loops for everyone
questions.explanation: The speaker says the group will meet at eight as planned.

questions.prompt: Who might add a second loop?
options: Anyone on a first visit
Runners training for the ten-kilometre race
People who forget a bottle
Only the coach and Jo
questions.explanation: The optional extra is for runners preparing for that distance.

questions.prompt: Where should participants go after the first loop if they do the second?
options: Along the path by the trees
Back towards the full-course signs
Across the bridge to the meeting point
Around the water tap
questions.explanation: The second-loop instructions specifically name the path by the trees.

questions.prompt: Why should a new runner speak to Jo?
options: To choose a longer race
To ask permission to drink water
To borrow a bottle for the next loop
So the group knows that runner has returned
questions.explanation: The coach expressly asks newcomers to check in when they finish.

children.segment_text: even if it is half full
